Iteration 3: with_skill 19/19 (100%), without_skill 18/19 (95%). Delta +0.05, down from iteration 2's +0.13 — because the two iteration-2 discriminators were narrowed: the webhooks fixture was made a true negative control (both configs now correctly pass it), and the new cross-module-reachin eval did not discriminate.

THE consistent discriminator, across iterations 2 and 3: business policy leaked into repository SQL (alerts eval, `attempts < MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS` in the where-clause). Only the skill run flags it; the baseline explicitly clears the repository as correct both times. This is anti-pattern 4, and it is the one finding unaided Claude reliably misses even with full repo access.

Negative control works: webhooks-clean passed 5/5 in BOTH configs — neither the skill nor the baseline fabricated a violation to justify a verdict. The skill did not make the model more trigger-happy.

Non-discriminating evals (2 of 4): reviewer-core-calibrate (domain purity — clock/RNG/env/prompt-slot) and cross-module-reachin (anti-pattern 7). In both, the baseline reads the real repo (prompt.ts, .dependency-cruiser.cjs, sibling modules) and reaches the same findings with the same fixes. The repo's own enforcement config and module conventions are effectively a second copy of the skill for these cases.
Cost collapsed too: +6s and +1.4k tokens (~+3%) this iteration — the skill's overhead is small when the fixtures are ones it actually helps on less.

Honest conclusion for the skill author: on realistic in-repo review with full context, this skill's measurable marginal value is narrow — it reliably adds the 'policy in the persistence ring' catch and sharpens rule-citation precision. Its larger value is likely in contexts this benchmark doesn't model: a cold agent with no repo access, or a reviewer who would not think to read .dependency-cruiser.cjs and server/src/ports/index.ts. A future iteration should test that scenario (restrict repo reads) to measure it.
Variance caveat unchanged: 1 run per cell; the +0.05 rests on a single assertion flip.
